subject: Order of Input in Genomic SEM Analysis

messages.author: 0e49334ffd28fb83
messages.subject: Order of Input in Genomic SEM Analysis
parts:
Dear all,

I have a question about the order of input indicators in Genomic SEM analysis. Initially, I used three variables: SBP (mmHg), DBP (mmHg), and PP (mmHg, defined as SBP-DBP), and constructed a common factor from these variables. However, since this common factor was almost identical to SBP, I began to wonder whether the order in which the variables are input might be affecting the results.

I understand that in commonfactorGWAS, the loading of the first indicator is set to 1. To address this, I tried using userGWAS to allow the first factor loading to be freely estimated (NA*), and also used ML estimation while only changing the order of inputs (Order 1: "SBP-DBP-PP" vs. Order 2: "PP-DBP-SBP"). Although I obtained the same LDSC matrix and sumstats, the final estimations were still not identical.

My question is: how can we eliminate the impact of the input order on the results as it's expected based on biological mechanisms?

Thank you very much in advance! I look forward to your guidance on this matter.

Best regards,
Yujia

messages.author: ac421cf36d1a4c37
messages.subject: Re: Order of Input in Genomic SEM Analysis
parts: Order just changes which indicator defaults to an unstandardized loading of 1 and will only change the metric of the factor gwas estimates, not the standardized estimates, z statistics, or p values of the snp effects on the factor.  Switching to a different estimator on the other hand will change these. We do not recommend the ML estimator these days.

sumstat2<-subset(sumstat2,sumstat2$CHR==1)

F1~SNP"

model2="F1=~NA*PP1+DBP1+SBP1
SBP1~~a*SBP1
a>0.001
F1~SNP"

BP2<-userGWAS(covstruc = LDSC2, SNPs = sumstat2, model = model2, sub=c("F1~SNP"),smooth_check=TRUE,fix_measurement=TRUE,Q_SNP=TRUE,parallel = FALSE)

save(BP1,BP2,file="userGWAS.RData")

parts: it doesn't look like you've specified an identified model. try fitting it without snps first. you have freed the loading of the first factor but not fixed the factor variance. you need a minimal identification constraint to set the metric of the factor.

Order just changes which indicator defaults to an unstandardized loading of 1 and will only change the metric of the factor gwas estimates, not the standardized estimates, z statistics, or p values of the snp effects on the factor.  Switching to a different estimator on the other hand will change these. We do not recommend the ML estimator these days.  


On Fri, Aug 30, 2024 at 9:42 AM 'Yujia Ma' via Genomic SEM Users <genomic-...@googlegroups.com> wrote:
Dear all,

I have a question about the order of input indicators in Genomic SEM analysis. Initially, I used three variables: SBP (mmHg), DBP (mmHg), and PP (mmHg, defined as SBP-DBP), and constructed a common factor from these variables. However, since this common factor was almost identical to SBP, I began to wonder whether the order in which the variables are input might be affecting the results.

I understand that in commonfactorGWAS, the loading of the first indicator is set to 1. To address this, I tried using userGWAS to allow the first factor loading to be freely estimated (NA*), and also used ML estimation while only changing the order of inputs (Order 1: "SBP-DBP-PP" vs. Order 2: "PP-DBP-SBP"). Although I obtained the same LDSC matrix and sumstats, the final estimations were still not identical.

My question is: how can we eliminate the impact of the input order on the results as it's expected based on biological mechanisms?

Thank you very much in advance! I look forward to your guidance on this matter.

Best regards,
Yujia
